answers.content: A honey bee colony typically contains one queen bee, seasonally up to a few thousand drone bees, and tens of thousands of female worker bees [S2]. The queen is usually one in number, while drones and workers are present in larger numbers [S2][S4]. Drones are produced from unfertilized eggs and are haploid, and workers are produced from fertilized eggs and are diploid [S2][S4]. Not all drones are produced from queen-laid eggs; rare instances of diploid drone larvae exist [S4]. The colony may contain as many as 60,000 worker bees [S1]. Drones are expelled during winter months [S4]. There is no mention of how many queens exist in a colony beyond the typical one [S2][S3].
